text: A few days ago, while I was scrolling Twitter, I came across this open source project called Roon, which was built by the same team behind OpenCode. Roon is an UI framework which is written completely in Rust. It uses its own custom GPU renderer, text engine, layout pipeline, and physics system to draw interfaces directly across macOS, Windows, Linux, and even web through WebAssembly. Developers are now using this Rust framework over Electron to build high-performance desktop apps since it is blazingly fast and extremely lightweight. Roon can also run headlessly, which means AI coding agents such as Cloud Code, Cursor, or Codex can render UI trees to PNGs behind the scenes, inspect element structures, and send programmatically-generated mouse and keyboard events to test to debug and build UI components completely on their own. So if you are building desktop apps and want the link to this GitHub repo, just comment Roon and I'll send it over.
